correctness.rationale: Every envy-free assignment on a triple indexed i<j<k must give its extremes to the two oppositely ranking agents and its middle to the third; this is feasible iff the third ranks that middle first on the triple. A three-case assignment construction guarantees at most one ordered envy edge for any triple, giving simultaneous exact minima of number of envious agents, ordered pairwise envy and maximum individual envy. Absence of middle-first triples is equivalent by induction to deleting only current interval endpoints from best to worst; there are exactly 2^(m-1) such orders. Conditional uniform third preferences yield the exact failure probability, and coherent prefix monotonicity gives the first-success distribution and its two moments by absolutely convergent tail sums. `check.py` independently enumerates all third-ranking permutations and all distinct assignments for m=3,...,8 and matches the exact objectives and first-success counts; finite checks are auxiliary, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating full text (Hosseini, Roy, Sethia, 2025, Section 4.2 Lemma 4.10) proves at most two unenvying agents when all rankings are single-dipped. That already implies the failure direction in the present setting, and is explicitly credited; the converse for two exactly opposed agents and the exact simultaneous three-objective and stock-size distributions are not given there. Gan, Suksompong, Voudouris (2019) provide a general existence decision algorithm and an unconditioned large-market asymptotic, not the restricted exact structural probability and stock law. Searches of accessible research records, accessible prior research claims, and primary literature did not find a covering exact statement; this is evidence of limited noncoverage, not definitive novelty proof.

value.rationale: The 2025 house-allocation research identifies minimizing envious agents as a motivated optimization task and treats single-dipped preferences as a natural restricted domain. A perfectly polarized two-agent pair creates a distinct extremal preference geometry. In that model the exact third-agent obstruction gives a full classification instead of a one-way impossibility lemma, and it simultaneously resolves the minima of all three standard envy objectives. The sharp factorial failure probability and finite expected house-stock threshold turn that structural obstruction into a natural finite-market quantity; neither is just a table of arbitrary small cases or a relabeling of the source theorem. This restricted classification has substantive benchmarking value even without broader policy or complexity claims.
